name: Updating an Element in the List (Case 3)
description: Construct a program that initializes a list with four string values, changes the last element in the list, and finally, prints the list.
code:
#Step 1: Define a list of four string values
lst = ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
#Step 2: Update the list elements
lst[3] = "e"
#Step 3: Print the list
print(lst)

comments.content: We want to assign four string values to the list. In this statement, we define the list referred by variable lst to hold four string values. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].
This statement, updates the last element of the list to string value "e".

To update an element in the list, we need to give the square bracket slice operator ([ ] ) along with an index of the element that we want to update on the left-hand side of the assignment operator. The index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the list. The value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator is the new value that we want to assign to the list element.
We can see the content of the list by calling the print function and passing list to that. This statement will print all the elements in the list.
